turns.text: /navigator Grill me on the message validation and retry work in this cycle. Start with validation.

Quick context first: `.standards/STATE.md` has this cycle in `DEVELOPING` with one open recovery frame (Tester reported that `sendMessage` makes four transport calls when three attempts are allowed), so I'll quiz you on the code as it currently stands in `src/validate.js` and `src/send.js`, not on the pending fix. Question 1: someone calls `sendMessage(transport, { to: 'ada', subject: '   ', body: 42 })`. Is the transport called, and what does the caller get back?

The transport isn't called. validateMessage finds three problems: the address has no @ and domain, the subject is only spaces so it counts as missing, and body isn't a string. sendMessage throws an InvalidMessageError carrying all three.

Correct on every point. `src/send.js` lines 26-27 run `validateMessage` and throw `InvalidMessageError` before the transport call on line 31, and `validateMessage` (`src/validate.js` lines 9-21) collects every problem instead of stopping at the first one, so `error.errors` is `['to must be an email address', 'subject is required', 'body must be a string']`. Question 2: a message has a valid address and body and a subject of 121 letters with no spaces. Which error or errors come back, and would a 120-letter subject pass?

Only one error, 'subject must be at most 120 characters'. The blank check passes because it isn't blank, so it falls through to the length check. Exactly 120 is fine since the check is greater than 120.

Right again. Line 13 of `src/validate.js` handles a missing or blank subject, and only otherwise does line 15 compare `message.subject.length > MAX_SUBJECT_LENGTH` (120, defined on line 3), so 121 letters gives exactly that one error and 120 passes. That covers input validation: you've shown that validation runs before any send, reports every problem at once, and where the subject limit sits. Next I'd move to what `sendMessage` does when the transport answers with a failure status. Shall I continue with that?
